rules.title: Char literal multi-byte UTF-8 decode
rules.statement: A char literal body whose first byte >= 0x80 is decoded as a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence: lead byte 110xxxxx => 2 bytes, 1110xxxx => 3, 11110xxx => 4; any other lead byte is an error ('invalid UTF-8'). Fewer than the required continuation bytes is an error ('truncated UTF-8'). The scalar value is the assembled code point.

rules.title: Char pattern scrutinee constraint
rules.statement: A char-literal pattern requires the scrutinee type to be `char` or an integer type; otherwise it is an error. The pattern matches the decoded code point as an integer constant.

rules.title: Char range pattern constraints
rules.statement: A char-range pattern `lo..=hi` requires a `char` or integer scrutinee, and requires lo <= hi (decoded code points); lo > hi is an error. It matches the inclusive integer range [lo, hi].

rules.title: Bool pattern scrutinee constraint
rules.statement: A boolean-literal pattern requires a `bool` scrutinee; any other (non-error) scrutinee type is an error.

rules.title: Tuple pattern over tuple or reference-to-tuple
rules.statement: A tuple pattern requires a tuple scrutinee, or a `&(T..)` / `&mut (T..)` scrutinee which is auto-dereferenced to the inner tuple (default binding mode). A non-tuple, non-(ref-to-tuple) scrutinee is an error.

rules.title: Tuple pattern `..` rest expansion
rules.statement: A tuple pattern may contain at most one `..` rest marker; a second `..` is an error. The rest is expanded into wildcard `_` skip entries inserted at the rest position so the explicit elements plus padding equal the tuple arity. More explicit elements than the arity (with `..`) is an error.

rules.title: Allowed tuple pattern element kinds
rules.statement: Tuple pattern elements may be: wildcard/binding (`_`/name), integer/negative-integer/bool/range literals, variant-data patterns, string literals, and or-patterns. Any other element kind is an error ('only _, name, integer, bool, range, or variant patterns are supported').

rules.title: String-literal tuple element lowered to str_eq guard
rules.statement: A string-literal element of a tuple pattern binds the element to a synthesized name and adds a refutable `str_eq(synth, lit)` guard, rather than a value-equality test (a raw `==` would pointer-compare). Requires the refutable-guard context to be active.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: tuple-arm codegen lacks a native str_eq dispatch, so string elements are desugared to guards.

rules.title: Single-alternative or-pattern element is unwrapped
rules.statement: The grammar wraps every tuple element in a PAT_OR node; a trivial single-alternative or-pattern is unwrapped and treated as its inner binding/wildcard/literal/variant. Multi-alternative or-patterns are kept as PatOr and their alternatives must be scalar (bindings inside multi-alt are dropped).

rules.title: Tuple pattern element count equals arity
rules.statement: After rest expansion, the number of tuple pattern elements must equal the tuple arity; a mismatch is an error.

rules.title: Default-ref binding for move-only tuple elements under shared borrow
rules.statement: When the tuple scrutinee is reached through a `&`/`&mut` (default binding mode), each tuple element binding whose element type is move-only (non-Copy, non-error, non-typevar) is bound by reference `&et`/`&mut et`; Copy elements are bound by value.

rules.title: Half-open range pattern clamps to scrutinee type bounds
rules.statement: In an integer range pattern, an omitted bound is clamped to the scrutinee integer type's min (for missing lo) or max (for missing hi); when the scrutinee type is unknown the bounds default to i32 range.

rules.title: Range pattern requires integer scrutinee
rules.statement: A range pattern requires an integer scrutinee type; a non-integer, non-error scrutinee is an error. A `never` scrutinee is exempted from this check.
rules.divergence: Logos char ranges are handled separately (PAT_CHAR_RANGE); PAT_RANGE is integer-only.

rules.title: Range pattern bounds must fit scrutinee type
rules.statement: Both bounds of an integer range pattern must fit within the scrutinee integer type; a bound that does not fit is an error.

rules.title: Exclusive range pattern lowered to inclusive minus one
rules.statement: An exclusive range pattern `lo..hi` is lowered as inclusive `lo..=(hi-1)`. An exclusive range with lo >= hi is an empty-range error. An inclusive range (default when unmarked) with lo > hi is an error.

rules.title: @-pattern binds whole value at scrutinee type
rules.statement: An `name @ subpat` pattern binds `name` to the whole scrutinee value at the scrutinee type (falling back to the error type if unknown) while also matching `subpat` against the same scrutinee type.

rules.title: Reference pattern requires reference scrutinee
rules.statement: A reference pattern `&pat`/`&mut pat` requires a reference scrutinee. `&mut pat` requires a `&mut` scrutinee; `&pat` accepts both `&` and `&mut`. A non-reference scrutinee is an error. The inner pattern is matched against the pointee type.

rules.title: `ref`/`ref mut` binding takes a reference to the matched place
rules.statement: A `ref x` / `ref mut x` binding binds `x` to a `&T` / `&mut T` reference of the scrutinee type `T` (the place's address) rather than moving the value.

rules.title: Bare identifier resolving to a no-payload enum variant is a variant pattern
rules.statement: When the scrutinee is an enum and a bare identifier (not `_`) names a no-payload variant of that enum, the identifier is treated as a variant pattern (refutable) rather than an irrefutable binding. This covers prelude variants (None/Some/Ok/Err) and user enums matched without the `Enum::` qualifier.
